objective: Create the perception spine: owner-consented one-shot screen snapshots ingested through the control plane, reduced in memory to privacy-preserving evidence, stored in a bounded monotonic-TTL freshness ledger, and surfaced on a new Dev Console page, with the OCR provider left as an honest contract-ready interface.
non_goals: Do not add automatic, scheduled or event-driven capture; every snapshot requires an explicit owner action.
Do not persist snapshot pixels, files or OCR text anywhere; only dimensions, hashes and luminance evidence may be retained in RAM.
Do not add an OCR or VLM dependency before it passes OSS/license review in a later M08 slice.
Do not let observations outlive their TTL or be presented as current context after expiry.
Do not bypass the safety policy: the perception feature flag and perception.observe capability gate every ingestion and fail closed.
base_sha: owner-records-at-commit (fast-development mode; slice authored in cloud sandbox without git access)
contracts: Every observation carries kind=screen.snapshot, trustLevel=untrusted, capturedAt, ttlSeconds<=15, expiresAt and monotonic-elapsed expiry; expired observations are excluded 100% of the time.
Snapshot ingestion calls safety evaluate on perception.observe with consume=true; deny fails closed, ask requires the explicit owner-confirmed header, and a crashing policy engine also fails closed.
The default capability manifest keeps the perception feature flag off, so capture is disabled until the owner enables it on the Safety page.
Snapshots are decoded from PNG in memory only; the service retains no pixel data, and the evidence payload is bounded and renderer-safe.
Local dedup (64-bit dHash) reports duplicates instead of creating new observations, and a monotonic sliding-window rate limit bounds ingestion.
Observations are evidence for the owner only in this slice; nothing feeds ContextBundle, chat prompts, memory or tools yet.
allowed_dependencies: Python standard library only (zlib PNG decode, hashlib, asyncio); no new Python or Node packages.
acceptance_criteria: Perception worker unit tests cover config bounds, PNG subset decoding and rejection, dHash dedup, rate limiting, TTL at T-epsilon/T/T+epsilon and fail-closed policy paths.

Control-plane route tests prove: feature flag off denies, ask requires owner confirmation, confirmed snapshots create TTL-bounded observations, duplicates are flagged, wrong content types are rejected, and a missing service fails closed.
Dev Console has a Quan sát page with explicit-consent capture via the browser display picker, an observation list with live TTL countdown, and honest OCR contract-ready labeling.
Fast unit suite, node --check on app.js and the Dev Console startup smoke stay green on the owner machine.
